title: Fix the Unchecked Command-Line Argument
description: The program should print the first command-line argument passed to it, or a usage message if none was given.
expectedBehavior: If an argument is provided, print it; otherwise print a usage message instead of crashing.
actualProblem: argv[1] is only valid if the program was actually given at least one command-line argument (argc >= 2). If it was run with none, argv[1] is NULL, and passing NULL to printf's %s specifier is undefined behavior (commonly a crash).
expectedOutput: Usage: <program name> <argument> (when run with no arguments), or 'First argument: <value>' when one is supplied.
explanation: argc tells you how many command-line arguments were actually provided, including the program name itself at argv[0]. Any code that reads argv[1] or beyond must first confirm argc is large enough.
